subject: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <data-procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines

Hi Mina,

Thanks for taking the time on the call last week. As we prepare our legal redlines to Redwood's DPA, procurement has asked for concrete evidence of the on‑shore erasure process and retention controls that support the proposed residency language (Section 5.2 and 8.1 in the redline). Specifically they want:

- A short, executable workflow showing how we will process a customer erasure request (steps, owners, SLAs).
- The retention windows that apply to cached KV and backups, and any exceptions.
- A sample audit/log extract demonstrating a prior successful erasure (obfuscated is fine).

Attached is our redline (we'll send an updated version with comments inline later). Can Redwood produce the artifacts above or point us to a standard evidence pack? If there are limitations (e.g., backup retention overlaps), call them out so we can track approval.

Appreciate a response by COB Wed (Aug 31) — procurement needs to decide if this moves to legal review.

Best,
Laura
Laura Chen
Senior Contracts Manager
Acme Corporation

Attachment: Acme_DPA_redline_v2.pdf (referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can provide the workflow and an obfuscated audit extract. There are a couple of nuances I want to flag up front so procurement has context:

- Backups: our standard managed backup retention for hosted customers is 30 days; Dedicated can be configured to shorter windows under contract.
- KV/cache: prefix/KV caches exist for live session performance and are evicted/rotated; we treat them as ephemeral but will include the eviction/TTL policy.
- Onshore erasure: for EU/US residency we provide regional wipe playbooks; for customers requiring an on‑site certified erase we have a manual process with a signed certificate.

I'll pull together a concise packet (workflow PDF, redaction of a real erasure log, and the playbook) and loop in product and legal for any language tweaks. Sending an internal note now.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Aug 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines

Team — forwarding Acme's request. They asked explicitly for: (1) erasure workflow with owners & SLAs; (2) retention windows for cache/backups; (3) obfuscated audit proving an erase.

Marissa — can you draft a 1‑page workflow (owner names as roles ok) and pull the standard playbook PDF. I attached our latest redline response (redline_dpa_v3.pdf) for reference.
Karthik — can you export a sanitized erasure log sample from the sandbox (remove customer ids, keep timestamps & operation IDs)? Also confirm backup retention for hosted vs dedicated and note any technical blockers to a <7 day backup retention option.

I'll coordinate delivery to Acme and map any redline language changes. Need both artifacts by EOD Tue so we can meet their Wed decision date.

Thanks — Mina

Attachment: redline_dpa_v3.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines

Mina — draft 1‑pager attached (erasure_flow_1pager.pdf) and I've summarized the retention bullets below so Acme has something concise for legal:

- Live caches (KV/prefix): TTL policy 0–24h depending on model & route; explicit session tokens flushed on user deletion requests — typical eviction within minutes to hours.
- Short‑term backups (managed/hosted): rolling backups retained 30 days; Dedicated customers can request contract amendment for 7/14/30 day options at purchase time.
- Long‑term archives/escrow snapshots: only retained when explicitly enabled for compliance; otherwise not created.

If Acme insists on a 7‑day mandatory backup retention across hosted, we should surface pricing/operational implications (higher job frequency, potential SLA adjustments). Karthik — marking for your numbers on the cost/SLO delta.

Attachment: erasure_flow_1pager.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2027 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines

Quick technical notes for the packet / for procurement: 

- We can produce an obfuscated erasure audit containing operation IDs, timestamps, and region tags; scrubbed of customer identifiers. Sample CSV (kms_audit_snapshot.csv) attached.
- Backup retention: hosted customers on standard plan are on 30d. We can offer 7d for Dedicated or as a paid tier for hosted (approx +18% infra cost for higher frequency snapshot policy). No technical blocker to a 7‑day window, but it requires contract-level provisioning and a small change in the backup orchestration job schedule.
- Onshore certified wipe: available for Dedicated deployments; for Hosted we provide region‑bound playbooks and a signed certificate of deletion after we perform multi‑region metadata verification.

I'll include a short blurb on how the erase request surfaces in the runtime (API call -> orchestrator -> KV flush -> snapshot invalidation -> backup tombstone) so legal can see chain of custody.

— Karthik

From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Procurement <data-procurement@acme-corp.com>, Tom Wells <tom.wells@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2027 15:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency & erasure evidence request — DPA redlines

Mina — thanks for the fast turnaround and the packet. The 1‑pager and obfuscated audit look good and procurement is comfortable moving the DPA to legal review with the following conditional ask: add a clause that allows Acme to request a 7‑day backup retention carve for our account (hosted) subject to an addendum and fee schedule. If Redwood is willing to add language committing to support that carve within 60 days of contract signature, legal will proceed to finalize.

Please send the final packet and I will route the redline back to my team with the conditional language request. If you can also attach the DocuSign ready DPA link we can get signatures in motion.

Best,
Laura

Attachment: summary_comments_acme.txt
Link: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/example-acme-dpa
